facts.label: Financial interpretation
facts.text: Net leverage rose in two steps. First, FY2025 reported EBITDA fell to USD 1,000 million from USD 1,887 million with debt little changed, which took net leverage from 3.38x to 6.05x; the fall includes a USD 381 million impairment of the TV Food Network investment and a year without election advertising, which is generally higher in even-numbered years. Second, the debt-financed acquisition lifted carrying debt to USD 11,409 million and net debt to USD 10,963 million while last-twelve-month reported EBITDA recovered to USD 1,597 million, leaving net leverage at 6.86x. Excluding the impairment, analyst arithmetic puts it at 5.54x. Neither figure is a covenant calculation, and the issuer reports lower ratios on its own definitions. facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Nexstar completed its cash acquisition of TEGNA on 2026-03-19 at $22 per share, a purchase price of USD 3,657 million for the equity and unvested awards. It added 64 television stations in 51 markets, the Premion advertising platform, two multicast networks and a podcast network, and the FCC approved the merger the same day with binding conditions. The conditions include a commitment to divest six stations within two years if the local ownership waiver is still needed and an offer to extend existing retransmission agreements at current rates until 2026-11-30. The annual report for 2025 values the transaction, agreed on 2025-08-18, at USD 6.2 billion including refinancing of certain TEGNA debt, fees and costs, against committed financing of up to USD 5.725 billion and a USD 125 million termination fee payable by Nexstar in specified cases. Those headline figures and the USD 3,657 million price measure different things, and the documents give no sources-and-uses table. facts.label: Key findings

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against caution is the issuer's own coverage and repayment record. It reports first-lien net leverage of 3.03x and total net leverage of 4.04x, repaid USD 1,311 million of debt since the start of 2026, generated USD 1,154 million of free cash flow in nine months and issued USD 5,115 million of notes in 2026 after the antitrust suits were filed, which shows that bond investors remained open to the credit. The 6.50% secured notes were valued at 96.14% of principal at quarter end by a bank's bid, which does not point to distress pricing. These points would win if the injunction were narrowed or lifted, if the first quarters of 2027 showed legacy non-political earnings growing and distribution revenue rising faster than subscribers fall, and if repayment continued while the dividend stayed flat, because the covenant average would then fall without relying on synergies.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: The credit's strengths start with a contractual distribution base. Distribution fees were USD 2,924 million in FY2025 against USD 2,928 million in FY2024 while advertising fell USD 456 million, because per-subscriber fees and annual escalators have outrun subscriber losses, so in the non-election year 59.08% of revenue held steady, and this is what carries fixed charges when political advertising is absent. The second strength is capital-light cash conversion: capital expenditure was 2.99% of FY2025 revenue and 2.05% in nine months of 2026, so most operating cash flow is available to repay debt, which is how USD 1,311 million was repaid in 2026. The third is liquidity and maturity shape: USD 887 million of cash and undrawn revolvers, both revolvers running to June 2030 and only 5.02% of principal due by the end of 2027 give the credit time to repay from cash flow. The fourth is demonstrated capital-markets access, with USD 5,115 million of notes issued after the antitrust suits were filed and a USD 1,750 million term loan raised at the March closing. The fifth is the absence of rating-downgrade triggers that accelerate maturities, so a rating action would raise cost and limit access rather than force repayment. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: The weaknesses start with leverage after a debt-funded acquisition: carrying debt rose USD 5,076 million to USD 11,409 million, and interest expense, net rose to USD 186 million in Q3 from USD 94 million a year earlier, so net interest absorbed 24.60% of Adjusted EBITDA even in the strongest quarter of 2026. The second is political cyclicality: with fixed operating costs, nearly every dollar of lost political revenue was lost operating profit in FY2025, which makes even-year earnings a poor guide to debt service. The third is dependence on a court and regulatory outcome that blocks the integration the price assumed, with no synergy size disclosed and the covenant window for counting synergies closing on 2027-09-19. The fourth is rate and refinancing cost: 42.61% of principal floats without hedges and the 2026 notes carry coupons of 6.50% and 7.25%. The fifth is shareholder and contingent-claim policy: a maintained dividend, a USD 1.4 billion repurchase authority, a USD 110 million minority put on The CW and unquantified litigation sit beside debt that is already high. facts.label: Company description and credit linkage
facts.text: Nexstar Media Group, Inc. is the listed parent of the largest local television station group in the United States by its own description, reaching about 80% of television households, and it also owns 82.0% of The CW, NewsNation and the Premion advertising platform and holds 31.3% of TV Food Network. The TEGNA acquisition closed on 2026-03-19, so the 2026 statements mix a legacy perimeter with a business owned for about six months. Revenue is 55.12% distribution, meaning retransmission and carriage fees paid per subscriber, and 44.06% advertising in nine months of 2026. The credit linkage is that per-subscriber fees are contractual and held steady through the non-election year, which supports debt service, whereas advertising carries the political cycle and drives the swing in coverage; the stations' network affiliations also tie cost to the networks' renewal terms. facts.label: Ownership, group structure and financial policy
facts.text: Figures are for Nexstar Media Group, Inc. consolidated, which includes the three independently owned station companies it consolidates as variable interest entities (Mission, White Knight and Vaughan) and The CW. The registrant has one class of common stock and no controlling holder named, so no sponsor stands behind or extracts from the credit, and the founder has been Chairman and Chief Executive Officer since 1996 with a term to 2029-03-31. Debt sits in several entities: Nexstar Media Inc. issues the 2028, 2033 secured and 2034 notes, Nexstar borrows under its own credit agreement, TEGNA issues the 2029 notes, Belo Corp. issues the two 2027 notes with TEGNA and Nexstar Media Group, Inc. as co-obligors, and Mission Broadcasting, an independently owned entity that Nexstar consolidates, borrows under its own facility that Nexstar guarantees. Mission guarantees the Nexstar facility and notes but not the notes assumed from TEGNA; The CW is excluded from the covenant group, the collateral and the guarantees, so its losses reduce consolidated earnings that the covenant ratio does not count. In nine months the obligor group's income from operations of USD 1,230 million exceeded the consolidated USD 1,159 million by USD 71 million. Financial policy was shareholder-friendly before the deal, with repurchases and dividends of USD 820 million in 2024 and USD 351 million in 2025, and has been more cautious since: no repurchases and debt repaid, with the dividend unchanged. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Distribution revenue is the larger and steadier stream: it was USD 3,044 million in nine months of 2026 against USD 2,204 million, of which USD 768 million came from TEGNA, with the legacy business adding USD 69 million from higher rates, streaming subscriber growth and the absence of a one-time charge in 2025, partly offset by subscriber attrition and the replacement of the CBS affiliation on six stations. Two customers represent 13% and 12% of revenue, which concentrates renewal risk in a small number of buyers, and the issuer states that subscriber losses could exceed contractual rate increases. Advertising revenue was USD 2,433 million in nine months of 2026, including political advertising of USD 511 million, 21.00% of advertising, against USD 25 million a year earlier; non-political advertising fell USD 25 million on political crowd-out and market softness. Distribution revenue was USD 1,091 million in Q3 against USD 1,116 million in Q2, a sequential decline of 2.24% with TEGNA in both quarters, and the filings do not discuss it, so it is a datapoint to watch rather than a trend. Revenue is therefore predictable in its distribution half, cyclical and partly discretionary in its advertising half, and concentrated in two customers, so credit gets only partial visibility through an odd year. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Costs are largely fixed. The issuer says a large percentage of its costs is relatively fixed, and the record shows it: in FY2025 revenue fell USD 458 million while direct operating and administrative costs fell USD 11 million, and in nine months of 2026 the legacy segment's programming and related expenses were USD 1,650 million against USD 1,646 million while its revenue rose USD 314 million. Margins are therefore defended by revenue, not by cost response, and the 94.32% decremental flow-through measured in FY2025 is an upper bound because that year's costs included merger legal fees, a disputed customer claim and refinancing costs; the 87.12% case removes the USD 33 million of one-time costs reported for nine months of 2025. Corporate unallocated costs rose to USD 212 million from USD 144 million and transaction and one-time expenses were USD 125 million, so integration costs weigh on 2026 cash flow while savings are blocked by the injunction. facts.label: Capital intensity and free cash flow conversion
facts.text: Capital intensity is low: capital expenditure was USD 148 million in FY2025 and USD 113 million in nine months of 2026, 2.05% of revenue, with no maintenance and growth split disclosed. Free cash flow conversion of Adjusted EBITDA was 62.04% in nine months of 2026 against 53.81% a year earlier, and Q3 unadjusted free cash flow of USD 634 million included a USD 258 million working-capital inflow that the issuer removes, which is why Adjusted Free Cash Flow of USD 443 million is the better run-rate guide. Cash interest and taxes together took USD 667 million of operating cash flow in nine months, and cash interest will rise further because the first coupon on the 2034 notes fell due on 2026-10-15, after the nine-month cash flow statement, and the 2026 debt will carry a full year of interest in 2027. About USD 100 million of operating cash flow came from distributions of TV Food Network, whose revenue fell 10.89% and whose partnership term ends on 2026-12-31 unless renewed, so part of the cash flow depends on an investee Nexstar does not control. Conversion is strong enough to repay debt in an election year and unproven in an odd one. facts.label: Industry forces
facts.text: Competition is intense and works through audience, programming and advertising, and the issuer names large technology and media groups as rivals for advertising. Its affiliation agreements with the four major networks limit its ability to license streaming distributors directly, so the networks negotiate with them. Entry requires government approvals, and the FCC voted on 2026-08-06 to repeal the national ownership cap, which would loosen limits on station groups generally, Nexstar included. Substitutes are streaming services that erode cable and satellite subscribers, which is the main pressure on the per-subscriber fee base. Buyer power sits with two customers at 13% and 12% of revenue and a local advertiser base of tens of thousands. Supplier power sits with the four major networks, whose affiliation agreements mostly expire through December 2027, when renewal may raise payments. The forces matter mostly through distribution and programming costs: a loss of leverage in either direction would show in the per-subscriber fee base and in fixed programming costs rather than in volume. facts.label: Regulatory, economic and technology factors
facts.text: Regulation is a primary credit driver here, so it is assessed: the FCC approved the merger on conditions that include divesting six stations within two years if a local ownership waiver is still needed, with no buyer agreed, and the notice on WPIX alleges an unauthorised transfer of control and proposes a forfeiture and a divestiture that the issuer disputes and cannot estimate; a challenge to the repeal of the national cap could bear on the injunction litigation because the merger relied on a waiver. Economic exposure runs through advertising softness and political crowd-out, with tariffs, inflation and high rates named as risks. Technology matters through streaming, which erodes the subscriber base, and through the next-generation broadcast standard, deployed in stations reaching 50% of households, for which no revenue is stated. Of the three, only regulation can force an asset sale, and the amounts are not established. facts.label: Opportunities and threats
facts.text: The strengths and weaknesses are set out above. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are a narrowed or lifted injunction that lets cost savings begin, a second year of repayment at the 2026 pace, the renewal of TV Food Network on current terms, and affiliation and retransmission renewals that keep rates ahead of subscriber losses. Threats that could weaken it are an adverse trial outcome that forces a divestiture or continued separation, a forfeiture and divestiture order on WPIX, a rise in MVPD attrition, higher network affiliation fees at the renewals through December 2027, refinancing of the 2027 notes of USD 440 million at higher cost, and the reversion of the covenant limit to 4.25x. facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: Scale and market position are strong: the largest station group by the issuer's description, reaching about 80% of households. Competitive advantage is average, resting on network affiliations and retransmission leverage that depend on renewals through December 2027. Business diversification is average: local advertising is spread over tens of thousands of advertisers and no market exceeds 3% of revenue, but two customers account for 25% of revenue and the business is one industry. Cost and capex flexibility is average, because capital expenditure is low yet operating costs are mostly fixed. Margin stability is weak, given the 94.32% decremental flow-through. Free cash flow stability is average, strong in an election year and unproven in an odd year on the new structure. The ability to refinance is average: markets were open for USD 5,115 million of notes in 2026, but at higher coupons and with 2027 maturities still to address. Liquidity is average, with USD 887 million available and no slack under a zero-cash-flow stress. Financial policy and governance are average, with repayment ahead of buybacks but an unchanged dividend and a board whose composition cannot be tested without the proxy statement. The trend is improving in cash terms and uncertain in earnings quality; the main missing datapoints are the covenant definitions, a post-acquisition odd-year result and peer comparisons. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: In the next 12 to 24 months the fourth quarter of 2026 should be the strongest of the cycle because political advertising peaks, after which 2027 loses it; the covenant election ends after 2026-12-31, the retransmission extension offered under the FCC condition ends on 2026-11-30, the Belo notes of USD 440 million mature on 2027-06-01 and 2027-09-15, the trial opens on 2027-07-06 and the outside synergies date is 2027-09-19. In three to five years the main items are the 2028 notes of USD 1,000 million and the Mission term loan, the 2030 revolver and Term Loan A, the effect of MVPD attrition against streaming growth, and whether deregulation allows further consolidation. Tailwinds are rate escalators, streaming subscriber growth, the completed CBS, FOX, ABC and CW affiliation renewals and any narrowing of the injunction; headwinds are the injunction, the odd-year drop, attrition and rising programming costs. Each supports or pressures cash-flow visibility and refinancing confidence rather than the near-term ability to pay. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The scenario starts in a non-election year with the injunction still in force at trial. First, political advertising falls from USD 511 million in the first nine months of 2026 to a residual, and at the FY2025 flow-through the combined business loses USD 423.39 million to USD 458.41 million of Adjusted EBITDA on a nine-month basis, leaving USD 1,401.59 million to USD 1,436.61 million. Second, interest does not fall: the 2026 structure carries about USD 558 million of net interest over nine months at the Q3 pace, so nine-month cover falls to 2.51x to 2.57x from 3.33x at the same interest pace. Third, free cash flow falls by the lost earnings less the tax saved while cash interest rises toward the run-rate of USD 706.83 million to USD 755.95 million a year, and the dividend of about USD 229.29 million a year continues unless cut. Fourth, liquidity of USD 887 million still covers the USD 579 million of principal due by the end of 2027, but not that plus the dividend and the minority put on The CW if free cash flow were zero, so the issuer would need free cash flow, a refinancing of the Belo notes, a dividend cut or the revolver. Fifth, the covenant limit reverts to 4.25x against 3.03x reported, which leaves 1.22x of headroom on the issuer's basis, so on the issuer's ratio a covenant breach is not the first break; the first breaks are interest cover and refinancing cost. Observable triggers are the ruling after the 2026-11-17 argument, the first two quarters of 2027, any second covenant election and the pricing of the 2027 notes. facts.label: Claims outside the debt figure
facts.text: The debt figure of USD 11,409 million excludes operating lease liabilities of USD 336 million, assumed programming commitments of USD 1,420 million that are not recorded as liabilities, the minority put on The CW with an estimated redemption value of USD 110 million against USD 28 million carried, and standby letters of credit of USD 30 million that reduce revolver availability. Pension and retiree funding is outside it too: Nexstar's own plans were underfunded by USD 154 million at 2025-12-31, the plan assumed from TEGNA carried a net liability of USD 19 million at closing and retiree plan funding obligations were USD 16 million at 2025-12-31. Before the acquisition, at 2025-12-31, Nexstar also had unrecorded commitments of USD 806 million under network affiliation agreements, USD 662 million falling due in 2026 and USD 144 million in 2027 to 2028, and USD 1,008 million of future broadcast rights commitments; these legacy figures sit beside the assumed commitments above and show that affiliation contracts largely run out by 2028, so renewal fees are not yet in them. The debt figure includes Mission's facility of USD 347 million, which Nexstar guarantees. Accrued network affiliation fees of USD 283 million and deferred revenue of USD 123 million are non-debt funding that grew with the acquisition. Litigation and tax items are unquantified: the Chicago Cubs tax matter on which the IRS proposed USD 182 million of tax and a USD 73 million penalty before a Tax Court decision for the company, the 2014 to 2015 audit adjustments, and the class action for money damages. The consent decrees carry no financial penalties. Searches of the filings found no factoring, supply-chain finance or finance lease disclosure. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Nexstar presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, a contractual per-subscriber fee base and low capital intensity, but credit quality is constrained by leverage taken on to buy TEGNA, by earnings that swing with the political cycle and by an integration that a court has blocked. Cash-flow durability appears adequate in election years and not yet established in odd years, because FY2025 showed a near-full flow-through of lost political revenue and the combined company has no odd-year record. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the pace of repayment through the first half of 2027, the outcome of the injunction litigation and the cost at which the 2027 notes and 2028 notes can be refinanced. The primary downside path is a non-election year with the injunction unresolved. No peer set was supplied, so the comparison with typical leveraged issuers in television broadcasting is a judgement: scale and the per-subscriber fee base are the differentiators and leverage at the election-year peak is the offset. Further analysis would require the covenant definitions, any court ruling after 2026-11-17, a post-acquisition odd-year result and peer comparisons. Fundamental credit assessment complete. Top risk: leverage that depends on election-year cash flow. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C05; calculation C07; calculation C13

## Findings
### Bottom line

The eight supplied filings and releases are sufficient for a credit snapshot of Nexstar's post-TEGNA capital structure and earnings, but not for covenant, priority or recovery conclusions, because no executed credit agreement or indenture was supplied.

Creditors should read every covenant, guarantee and ranking statement as the issuer's own summary. The latest evidence is dated 2026-11-05, so the outcome of an appeal hearing that the third-quarter report schedules between its filing date and the as-of date is not reported. No credit ratings, market quotes, peer set, management projections or fund limits were supplied, so the work that needs them is conditional.

## Gaps

- Material: The executed credit agreements and indentures are not supplied. The exhibit indexes list the 2017 credit agreements of Nexstar and Mission with their amendments through the 2026 amendments, the 2019 and 2020 indentures for the unsecured notes, and the 2026 indentures for the secured notes due 2033 and the unsecured notes due 2034; the notes assumed from TEGNA are described only in the quarterly reports. Covenant definitions, baskets, restricted-payment limits, guarantee releases, collateral and priority can therefore be read only from the issuer's summaries, so Legal & covenants, Covenant capacity, Structural priority, Intercreditor control, Recovery & fulcrum and Security selection stay conditional. The remedy is to supply those executed documents.

- Material: No credit rating, agency report, trading quote or peer financials are supplied. The filings state only that no downgrade triggers accelerate maturities and that a downgrade could affect refinancing access, and the notes give quarter-end fair values of debt from third-party bid prices rather than quotes at the as-of date. Agency views, market-implied pricing and peer comparison are therefore not established, and Ratings & triggers, Market-implied risk and Peer benchmark stay conditional.

- Minor: Evidence after 2026-11-05 is not supplied. The third-quarter report describes an appeal hearing as scheduled after its own filing date, and the sources do not say whether it took place or what the court decided, so the injunction on integrating TEGNA is described as in force only as of that filing. A later filing or release would close this.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C01

- Minor: Directors, executive pay, security ownership and related-party transactions are incorporated by reference from the proxy statement, which is not supplied; the second-quarter report cites a definitive proxy statement filed in April 2026. Only the executive officer list is printed, so governance conclusions beyond that list need the proxy statement.

- Minor: No management projections, synergy targets, guidance or management bridge are supplied, the run inputs hold no forecast or downside assumptions, and no portfolio or fund limits are supplied. Forward and downside work would rest on reported history and stated analyst assumptions, and the committee decision cannot state the fund's constraints.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4

- Minor: The issuer-reported leverage ratios are not one series. The first-quarter release adjusted the ratio for run-rate cost savings and contractual retransmission revenues expected within 18 months of a transaction, while the second-quarter and third-quarter releases exclude the synergies expected from the TEGNA acquisition; the ratio also uses an average of the last two years of EBITDA on a pro forma basis. The three ratios should not be read as a trend without restating, and the credit agreement definitions behind them are not supplied.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-07_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4

- Minor: The annual report states a transaction value of USD 6.2 billion before closing, including refinancing of TEGNA debt, fees and costs, while the quarterly report states a purchase price of USD 3.7 billion for the equity, with USD 2,559 million of debt assumed shown separately. They are different definitions and must not be blended.

- Minor: Three small differences inside the supplied documents are not reconciled by the sources. The third-quarter report gives a notice of appeal in April 2026 in the litigation note and risk factors but an appeal filed in May 2026 in the acquisition note. The earnings release reports nine-month debt repayment of USD 786 million against USD 783 million of repaid principal under the senior secured facilities in the quarterly report, a difference of USD 3 million. The collateral for the assumed 2027 notes is described in the third-quarter report both as secured by the company and as secured by certain assets of Belo Corp. and its subsidiaries, after the first-quarter report said the company intended to secure them. Both versions are kept.

## Findings
### Bottom line

The TEGNA acquisition lifted carrying debt from USD 6,333 million at year-end 2025 to USD 11,409 million, leaving net leverage at 6.86x on reported last-twelve-month EBITDA, so creditors depend on a full year of TEGNA earnings and continued repayment.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nxst-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C01; calculation C05

The issuer's own covenant ratios are far lower, at 3.03x first lien and 4.04x total net, because they count TEGNA for a full period and use a different EBITDA; this module cannot reproduce that basis. Adjusted EBITDA is stated only for interim periods, and FY2025 reported EBITDA carries a USD 381 million impairment, so every leverage figure here is a reported-basis ceiling, not a forecast. The dividend payable on 2026-11-27 would lift net leverage to 6.90x.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C09; calculation C11; calculation C12

### Financial interpretation

Net leverage rose in two steps. First, FY2025 reported EBITDA fell to USD 1,000 million from USD 1,887 million with debt little changed, which took net leverage from 3.38x to 6.05x; the fall includes a USD 381 million impairment of the TV Food Network investment and a year without election advertising, which is generally higher in even-numbered years. Second, the debt-financed acquisition lifted carrying debt to USD 11,409 million and net debt to USD 10,963 million while last-twelve-month reported EBITDA recovered to USD 1,597 million, leaving net leverage at 6.86x. Excluding the impairment, analyst arithmetic puts it at 5.54x. Neither figure is a covenant calculation, and the issuer reports lower ratios on its own definitions.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nxst-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 92; 10-K_2025-12-31_nxst-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; calculation C05; calculation C11

Cash interest paid over the last twelve months is USD 526 million and reported EBITDA covers it 3.04x, down from 4.38x in FY2024. Accrued net interest of USD 495 million for nine months in 2026 against USD 288 million a year earlier shows the new debt costing more than the debt it replaced, and cash paid should rise because the first coupon of the 2033 secured notes fell due in September 2026 and that of the 2034 notes in October 2026, after the nine-month cash flow statement, so most of a full year of new coupons is still to come.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C04; calculation C05

Free cash flow rose to USD 1,154 million for nine months from USD 607 million a year earlier, after operating cash flow of USD 1,267 million and capital expenditure of USD 113 million, and the issuer applied it to USD 783 million of facility repayments and USD 171 million of dividends. Working-capital inflows of USD 128 million from receivables and USD 89 million from accruals contributed, and advertising revenue is generally higher in even-numbered election years, so the 2026 cash flow is not a run rate for odd years.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; calculation C08

Liquidity is adequate for near-term maturities: cash of USD 446 million and undrawn revolving commitments of USD 441 million total USD 887 million against USD 28 million of principal due in the rest of 2026 and USD 551 million in 2027, which includes the assumed 2027 notes. The revolver and the Term Loan A mature in 2030, so the wall of larger maturities sits beyond the next two years. Revolver availability depends on the covenant tests, whose definitions are not supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation C03; calculation C07

Two non-debt obligations grew with the acquisition and fund operations without bearing interest: accrued network affiliation fees rose to USD 283 million from USD 77 million and deferred revenue rose to USD 123 million from USD 24 million. A slowdown in distribution or advertising receipts, or tighter network terms, would hit cash before reported debt changes, so these balances should be tracked beside debt. Repayments of USD 525 million after the quarter end leave net debt unchanged at the event itself and do not reflect cash generated in October and November.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation C03

The strongest contrary evidence is that the issuer reports a first lien net leverage of 3.03x and total net leverage of 4.04x against a covenant test of 4.75x, and that it has repaid USD 1.3 billion of debt since the start of the year. Those figures would win if the issuer's two-year EBITDA average and full pro forma TEGNA earnings were the right measure of creditor exposure; this module cannot confirm that because the credit agreement is not supplied. A downside runs from an adverse ruling in the pending merger litigation, which could force divestitures or keep TEGNA separate, through lower synergies and EBITDA, to higher leverage against 2027 maturities; the observable triggers are the appeal outcome and the next quarterly leverage ratio.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C07

- Low: The legal parent, the borrower and the note issuers are different entities; the guarantee and restricted-group perimeters are summarised in the filings but the executed documents are not supplied, so the consolidated statements are not tied to a restricted-group perimeter.

spans.text: ## Request

Business & governance for Nexstar Media Group, Inc. (nxst-1142417) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the TEGNA acquisition and its financing, the business and operating model, ownership and control, governance and capital-allocation behaviour, and dated events, taken from the 2025 annual report, the 2026 quarterly reports and the 2026 earnings releases. It uses the accepted source-readiness answer for the document perimeter and calculates no financial-foundation ratios.

No external sources were used. Dates above are the signature or release dates the documents state.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Governance risk for creditors is medium: Nexstar directs cash to debt repayment, but the debt-funded TEGNA acquisition sits under a court order barring integration, so creditors must rely on cash flow, not synergies, for deleveraging.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; Source readiness (CP-0)

The acquisition cost USD 3,657 million for the equity and lifted carrying debt from USD 6,333 million at year-end 2025 to USD 11,409 million at 2026-09-30. Nexstar repaid USD 786 million in nine months against USD 171 million of dividends, and USD 525 million more after quarter end, yet kept its dividend at $1.86 per share. No controlling holder is named, so risk comes from the founder-led management, contract-based control of independent station owners and dependence on regulators and courts.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C05; calculation C08; calculation C09
### Key findings

- Ownership gives creditors no sponsor to rely on or to fear: the stock is a single class with one vote per share, no preferred stock is outstanding and no controlling holder is named, but holder percentages and board composition are not established because they sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nxst-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-K_2025-12-31_nxst-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-K_2025-12-31_nxst-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-K_2025-12-31_nxst-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 135; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Management continuity is a strength with a key-person edge: the founder has led the company as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer since 1996, his term runs to 2029-03-31, and the issuer itself lists his loss as a risk, so execution of the acquisition rests heavily on one executive.

- The TEGNA acquisition is the dominant governance fact: it was funded by new debt, carrying debt rose by USD 5,076 million in nine months, and a court order in force since 2026-04-21 stops integration, so the synergies that justified the price cannot be relied on before the trial on 2027-07-06.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C08

- Capital allocation has turned toward deleveraging without pausing the dividend: debt repayment was 4.60x dividends in nine months and no shares were repurchased, but the board declared the unchanged dividend on 2026-10-30 and USD 1.4 billion of repurchase authority remains, so repayment discipline is behavioural and not contractual.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation C09; calculation C10

- Control of independent stations is contractual and exposed to regulators: Nexstar consolidates 35 of the 37 stations owned by independent parties through service agreements, a guarantee of Mission's USD 347 million of principal and purchase options, and the FCC's 2024 notice over station WPIX alleges an unauthorised transfer of control with a proposed forfeiture and a required divestiture that Nexstar disputes and cannot estimate.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C14

- The business is more cyclical in 2026 than its mix suggests: distribution is the larger and steadier stream at 55.12% of nine-month revenue, but election-year political advertising supplied USD 511 million, 21.00% of advertising, and falls away in odd-numbered years, as the USD 25 million of nine-month 2025 political revenue showed, while two customers account for 13% and 12% of revenue.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C12

- Regulation is both the enabler and the exposure: FCC approval carried binding conditions including a possible six-station divestiture, and the FCC's vote on 2026-08-06 to repeal the national ownership rule, not yet effective, could be challenged in ways the issuer says may affect the TEGNA litigation.

- Disclosure is adequate for monitoring but incomplete for control analysis: quarterly reports and earnings releases are timely and internal control over financial reporting was effective at year-end 2025, but the purchase price allocation is preliminary and the executed debt documents that set dividend and investment capacity are not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nxst-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for lower risk is cash generation and visible deleveraging: Adjusted Free Cash Flow was USD 1,101 million in nine months, debt repayments were USD 786 million, the company reports compliance with its financial covenants, and the issuer's first-lien ratio of 3.03x sits well inside the 4.75x test with total net leverage of 4.04x. Both ratios use credit agreement definitions that average two years of EBITDA and exclude TEGNA synergies from the second quarter, so they are not comparable with leverage on reported figures and do not by themselves lower the view.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-07_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C18

The view would improve to low if the appeal or the 2027 trial lifted the injunction, repayment continued at the nine-month pace while the dividend stayed flat, and no divestiture or forfeiture followed. It would worsen to high if the courts ordered divestitures or a longer hold-separate period, if a challenge to the ownership-rule repeal undermined the waiver, if repurchases resumed before leverage fell, or if the WPIX proceeding ended in a forfeiture and a divestiture order.
### Limitations

- Directors, committees, pay and holders above any reporting threshold are in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so the conclusion that no controlling holder is named cannot be confirmed, and a concentrated holder would raise the governance risk level.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nxst-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-K_2025-12-31_nxst-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 82; Source readiness (CP-0)
- The purchase price allocation is preliminary for up to twelve months after closing, so the goodwill share of the price and the identifiable intangible assets behind the new debt could still move.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C05

- The executed credit agreements and indentures are not supplied, so dividend, repurchase and investment capacity under them is not established; the capital-allocation view rests on observed behaviour only and would change if the baskets proved wide.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; Source readiness (CP-0)

- No synergy target, sources-and-uses statement or post-acquisition rating action is supplied, so the judgement that deleveraging depends on cash flow rather than savings rests on the issuer's removal of synergies from its covenant calculation, not on a measured shortfall.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Nexstar completed its cash acquisition of TEGNA on 2026-03-19 at $22 per share, a purchase price of USD 3,657 million for the equity and unvested awards. It added 64 television stations in 51 markets, the Premion advertising platform, two multicast networks and a podcast network, and the FCC approved the merger the same day with binding conditions. The conditions include a commitment to divest six stations within two years if the local ownership waiver is still needed and an offer to extend existing retransmission agreements at current rates until 2026-11-30. The annual report for 2025 values the transaction, agreed on 2025-08-18, at USD 6.2 billion including refinancing of certain TEGNA debt, fees and costs, against committed financing of up to USD 5.725 billion and a USD 125 million termination fee payable by Nexstar in specified cases. Those headline figures and the USD 3,657 million price measure different things, and the documents give no sources-and-uses table.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nxst-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_nxst-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-03-31_nxst-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C05; calculation C06

The acquisition was financed with new debt. In March 2026 Nexstar drew USD 148 million on its revolver, USD 150 million of a 2027 Term Loan A and USD 1,750 million of a 2033 Term Loan B at SOFR plus 2.75%, and issued USD 3,390 million of 6.50% secured notes due 2033 on 2026-03-25; temporary bridge loans of USD 1,211 million were repaid in March. On 2026-04-02 it issued USD 1,725 million of 7.25% unsecured notes due 2034 to redeem its 2027 unsecured notes. New borrowings at closing total USD 5,438 million, USD 287 million below the commitment ceiling, and carrying debt rose from USD 6,333 million at year-end 2025 to USD 11,409 million at 2026-09-30, an increase of USD 5,076 million.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C07; calculation C08

Nexstar assumed TEGNA debt at a fair value of USD 2,559 million and repaid most of it: USD 1,000 million of senior unsecured notes at par under a call right and USD 1,040 million of the 2029 notes by tender offer, which leaves USD 60 million of those notes outstanding. USD 440 million of 2027 notes issued by Belo Corp., with TEGNA and Nexstar as co-obligors, remain and were secured after closing.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C07

The credit agreement lets Nexstar raise its maximum first-lien net leverage ratio from 4.25x to 4.75x after a material transaction; Nexstar made that election from the first quarter of 2026 and the higher limit remains in effect through 2026-12-31, with at most two such elections allowed. At 2026-09-30 the issuer reports 3.03x first-lien and 4.04x total net leverage on credit agreement definitions that exclude The CW, average two years of EBITDA, assume TEGNA was owned for the full period and, from the second quarter, exclude expected TEGNA synergies because the injunction limits their delivery. The first-quarter first-lien ratio of 2.94x included expected run-rate savings and is not comparable with 3.21x for the second quarter and 3.03x for the third.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4

State attorneys general and DIRECTV sued on 2026-03-18 to stop the merger; the court entered a hold-separate order on 2026-03-27 and a preliminary injunction on 2026-04-17, effective 2026-04-21, prohibiting further integration. Nexstar appealed but did not seek a stay and says it has abided by the order; a special master was appointed on 2026-08-28 and trial is set for 2027-07-06. Oral argument on the appeal was scheduled for 2026-11-17, the day before the as-of date. Adverse outcomes could require divestitures, continued separation or modified integration plans.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 32–34; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3

After the quarter end Nexstar repaid USD 400 million on 2026-10-30 and USD 125 million on 2026-11-05 of principal under its senior secured credit facilities, and on 2026-10-30 its board declared the usual quarterly dividend of $1.86 per share payable on 2026-11-27 to holders of record on 2026-11-13. These subsequent events are not in the 2026-09-30 balance sheet. The issuer's unaudited pro forma disclosure, as if the merger had occurred on 2025-01-01, shows nine-month 2026 net revenue of USD 6,133 million against reported USD 5,522 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation C09; calculation C15

Earlier transactions were smaller: the WBNX-TV station in Cleveland for USD 22 million on 2025-01-31 and, in September 2022, The CW network for no consideration. The larger Tribune acquisition closed on 2019-09-19 and left tax contingencies that the company still carries, and the senior secured credit facilities were refinanced on 2025-06-27.

spans.text: ## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for Nexstar Media Group, Inc. (nxst-1142417) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway, first run of this pathway. Scope is the consolidated business, financial profile, debt and claims outside debt, liquidity, covenant position, outlook and downside, built from the eight supplied filings and releases and the three earlier analyses of this run. It assigns no rating, sizes no position and recommends no security.
## Sources

No external sources were used. Dates above are the signature or release dates the documents state.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Nexstar's credit is stretched rather than impaired: near-term liquidity and a back-ended maturity profile protect creditors, but leverage rests on election-year cash flow that falls away in 2027, so the 2026 repayment pace should not be extrapolated.

Net debt was USD 10,963 million at 2026-09-30, 6.86x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA; pro forma for the dividend payable on 2026-11-27 it is USD 11,020.33 million and 6.90x. The issuer's first-lien ratio of 3.03x against a 4.75x limit rests on a definition that cannot be reproduced here. Political advertising matches the whole of the legacy business's 2026 earnings growth, so USD 1,311 million repaid since the start of 2026 says little about 2027.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C06; calculation C11
### Key findings

- Leverage is the central weakness, and no single measure fixes it. Net debt over last-twelve-month reported EBITDA was 6.86x at 2026-09-30 (6.90x pro forma for the dividend payable on 2026-11-27), against 3.38x at the end of FY2024 and 6.05x at the end of FY2025; excluding the USD 381 million equity-investment impairment it is 5.54x. The issuer's 4.04x total net ratio counts a full year of TEGNA, averages an election year with a non-election year and excludes The CW, so it is closer to through-cycle leverage in concept but cannot be verified from the documents.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-05-07_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4

- Cash generation is strong and is the only deleveraging source for now. Nine-month 2026 free cash flow was USD 1,154 million, 62.04% of issuer Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,860 million, with capital expenditure at 2.05% of revenue; the issuer repaid USD 786 million of debt and paid USD 171 million of dividends in the period and a further USD 525 million of facility principal after the quarter end.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; calculation C09; calculation C11

- The 2026 earnings step-up is political and acquired, not underlying. Legacy Adjusted EBITDA rose USD 271 million in nine months against a USD 274 million rise in legacy political advertising, and the non-election year FY2025 showed the reverse: revenue fell USD 458 million and operating EBITDA (income from operations before depreciation and amortization) fell USD 432 million, a 94.32% flow-through, because direct operating and administrative costs fell only USD 11 million.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nxst-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-K_2025-12-31_nxst-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C05; calculation C06

- The first odd year on the new capital structure is the main test of interest cover. Removing the nine-month political swing at the FY2025 flow-through leaves Adjusted EBITDA near USD 1,401.59 million, which covers nine months of interest at the Q3 pace 2.51x, against 3.33x for the actual 2026 Adjusted EBITDA at the same pace and 3.76x on interest actually accrued; a lower flow-through of 87.12% gives 2.57x. Run-rate interest of USD 706.83 million to USD 755.95 million a year is 34.38% to 43.72% above the USD 526 million of cash interest paid in the last twelve months.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C07; calculation C08

- Liquidity covers scheduled needs but has no slack if free cash flow stopped. Cash of USD 446 million and undrawn revolvers of USD 441 million total USD 887 million, against USD 579 million of principal due by the end of 2027 and USD 286.61 million of dividends; adding the USD 110 million minority put on The CW, the shortfall would be USD 88.61 million, so 2027 relies on free cash flow or refinancing.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C10

- Maturities are back-ended but the cost of capital has risen. Only 5.02% of principal falls due by the end of 2027 and 65.36% after 2031, yet the notes issued to refinance the 2027 unsecured notes carry a higher coupon, 42.61% of principal floats with no hedges and a 100 bp rise in SOFR would add USD 49 million of annual interest.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-K_2025-12-31_nxst-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 121; calculation C01; calculation C12

- Covenant headroom is wide on the issuer's definition and narrows in 2027. The only financial maintenance covenant the filings describe is a first-lien net leverage limit of 4.75x, which reverts to 4.25x after 2026-12-31 unless a further material transaction allows a second election; the issuer reports 3.03x, a gap of 1.72x now and 1.22x against the lower limit, but the earnings cushion is not calculable without the credit agreement definitions.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C13

- The court and regulatory process decides whether TEGNA can be integrated, and creditors cannot count on synergies. The preliminary injunction has barred integration since 2026-04-21, trial is set for 2027-07-06 and the covenant counts synergies only if they are expected by 2027-09-19, so the issuer removed them from its ratios; the commitment to divest six stations and the FCC notice on WPIX add disposal risk that cannot be sized.

- Shareholder policy is moderate in cost but discretionary in direction. The dividend of $1.86 per share a quarter costs about USD 229.29 million a year and no shares were repurchased in 2026, yet USD 1.4 billion of repurchase authority remains and the minority put on The CW adds a USD 110 million cash call against USD 28 million carried.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C10
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against caution is the issuer's own coverage and repayment record. It reports first-lien net leverage of 3.03x and total net leverage of 4.04x, repaid USD 1,311 million of debt since the start of 2026, generated USD 1,154 million of free cash flow in nine months and issued USD 5,115 million of notes in 2026 after the antitrust suits were filed, which shows that bond investors remained open to the credit. The 6.50% secured notes were valued at 96.14% of principal at quarter end by a bank's bid, which does not point to distress pricing. These points would win if the injunction were narrowed or lifted, if the first quarters of 2027 showed legacy non-political earnings growing and distribution revenue rising faster than subscribers fall, and if repayment continued while the dividend stayed flat, because the covenant average would then fall without relying on synergies.

The view would turn more cautious if the Ninth Circuit or the 2027 trial left the injunction in force through the outside synergies date, if the first odd-year quarters on the new structure showed cover below the 2.51x illustrated here, if the issuer's first-lien ratio rose above 3.03x while the limit reverted to 4.25x, if repurchases resumed before leverage fell, or if the 2027 notes of USD 440 million had to be refinanced at materially higher cost.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C07; calculation C12; calculation C14
### Limitations

- No post-acquisition odd-year result exists, because TEGNA has been consolidated only since 2026-03-19 and only in an election year, so the interest-cover sensitivity applies the legacy business's FY2025 cost behaviour to the combined company; if TEGNA's costs are more variable the odd-year cover would be better than the 2.51x to 2.57x shown, and if less variable, worse.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nxst-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C07

- The liquidity stress and the run-rate interest range are constructions from stated assumptions, not forecasts: the stress sets free cash flow to zero and the interest range applies the term-loan rate band to every floating balance, so they size the 2027 funding conclusion without predicting it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation C03; calculation C04

- The covenant conclusion rests on a ratio the issuer computes and no compliance certificate or executed definition was supplied, so headroom is stated in turns of leverage only and the fall in earnings that would breach the test is not calculable.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C13

- Two exposures are unquantified and sit outside every leverage figure here: the class action on local advertising pricing, with trial set for 2027-11-01, and the dispute over the 2009 Chicago Cubs transactions, where the IRS has appealed a Tax Court decision that found no tax due; either could add a cash claim that the liquidity and claims conclusions do not include.

- No peer set or sector benchmark was supplied, so the strong, average and weak grades in this analysis are absolute judgements on the issuer's own history and terms; peer leverage and cover could move the grades for scale, competitive position and refinancing capacity.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)
### Strengths and weaknesses

The credit's strengths start with a contractual distribution base. Distribution fees were USD 2,924 million in FY2025 against USD 2,928 million in FY2024 while advertising fell USD 456 million, because per-subscriber fees and annual escalators have outrun subscriber losses, so in the non-election year 59.08% of revenue held steady, and this is what carries fixed charges when political advertising is absent. The second strength is capital-light cash conversion: capital expenditure was 2.99% of FY2025 revenue and 2.05% in nine months of 2026, so most operating cash flow is available to repay debt, which is how USD 1,311 million was repaid in 2026. The third is liquidity and maturity shape: USD 887 million of cash and undrawn revolvers, both revolvers running to June 2030 and only 5.02% of principal due by the end of 2027 give the credit time to repay from cash flow. The fourth is demonstrated capital-markets access, with USD 5,115 million of notes issued after the antitrust suits were filed and a USD 1,750 million term loan raised at the March closing. The fifth is the absence of rating-downgrade triggers that accelerate maturities, so a rating action would raise cost and limit access rather than force repayment.

### Company description and credit linkage

Nexstar Media Group, Inc. is the listed parent of the largest local television station group in the United States by its own description, reaching about 80% of television households, and it also owns 82.0% of The CW, NewsNation and the Premion advertising platform and holds 31.3% of TV Food Network. The TEGNA acquisition closed on 2026-03-19, so the 2026 statements mix a legacy perimeter with a business owned for about six months. Revenue is 55.12% distribution, meaning retransmission and carriage fees paid per subscriber, and 44.06% advertising in nine months of 2026. The credit linkage is that per-subscriber fees are contractual and held steady through the non-election year, which supports debt service, whereas advertising carries the political cycle and drives the swing in coverage; the stations' network affiliations also tie cost to the networks' renewal terms.

### Ownership, group structure and financial policy

Figures are for Nexstar Media Group, Inc. consolidated, which includes the three independently owned station companies it consolidates as variable interest entities (Mission, White Knight and Vaughan) and The CW. The registrant has one class of common stock and no controlling holder named, so no sponsor stands behind or extracts from the credit, and the founder has been Chairman and Chief Executive Officer since 1996 with a term to 2029-03-31. Debt sits in several entities: Nexstar Media Inc. issues the 2028, 2033 secured and 2034 notes, Nexstar borrows under its own credit agreement, TEGNA issues the 2029 notes, Belo Corp. issues the two 2027 notes with TEGNA and Nexstar Media Group, Inc. as co-obligors, and Mission Broadcasting, an independently owned entity that Nexstar consolidates, borrows under its own facility that Nexstar guarantees. Mission guarantees the Nexstar facility and notes but not the notes assumed from TEGNA; The CW is excluded from the covenant group, the collateral and the guarantees, so its losses reduce consolidated earnings that the covenant ratio does not count. In nine months the obligor group's income from operations of USD 1,230 million exceeded the consolidated USD 1,159 million by USD 71 million. Financial policy was shareholder-friendly before the deal, with repurchases and dividends of USD 820 million in 2024 and USD 351 million in 2025, and has been more cautious since: no repurchases and debt repaid, with the dividend unchanged.

### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Distribution revenue is the larger and steadier stream: it was USD 3,044 million in nine months of 2026 against USD 2,204 million, of which USD 768 million came from TEGNA, with the legacy business adding USD 69 million from higher rates, streaming subscriber growth and the absence of a one-time charge in 2025, partly offset by subscriber attrition and the replacement of the CBS affiliation on six stations. Two customers represent 13% and 12% of revenue, which concentrates renewal risk in a small number of buyers, and the issuer states that subscriber losses could exceed contractual rate increases. Advertising revenue was USD 2,433 million in nine months of 2026, including political advertising of USD 511 million, 21.00% of advertising, against USD 25 million a year earlier; non-political advertising fell USD 25 million on political crowd-out and market softness. Distribution revenue was USD 1,091 million in Q3 against USD 1,116 million in Q2, a sequential decline of 2.24% with TEGNA in both quarters, and the filings do not discuss it, so it is a datapoint to watch rather than a trend. Revenue is therefore predictable in its distribution half, cyclical and partly discretionary in its advertising half, and concentrated in two customers, so credit gets only partial visibility through an odd year.

### Cost structure and margin resilience

Costs are largely fixed. The issuer says a large percentage of its costs is relatively fixed, and the record shows it: in FY2025 revenue fell USD 458 million while direct operating and administrative costs fell USD 11 million, and in nine months of 2026 the legacy segment's programming and related expenses were USD 1,650 million against USD 1,646 million while its revenue rose USD 314 million. Margins are therefore defended by revenue, not by cost response, and the 94.32% decremental flow-through measured in FY2025 is an upper bound because that year's costs included merger legal fees, a disputed customer claim and refinancing costs; the 87.12% case removes the USD 33 million of one-time costs reported for nine months of 2025. Corporate unallocated costs rose to USD 212 million from USD 144 million and transaction and one-time expenses were USD 125 million, so integration costs weigh on 2026 cash flow while savings are blocked by the injunction.

### Industry forces

Competition is intense and works through audience, programming and advertising, and the issuer names large technology and media groups as rivals for advertising. Its affiliation agreements with the four major networks limit its ability to license streaming distributors directly, so the networks negotiate with them. Entry requires government approvals, and the FCC voted on 2026-08-06 to repeal the national ownership cap, which would loosen limits on station groups generally, Nexstar included. Substitutes are streaming services that erode cable and satellite subscribers, which is the main pressure on the per-subscriber fee base. Buyer power sits with two customers at 13% and 12% of revenue and a local advertiser base of tens of thousands. Supplier power sits with the four major networks, whose affiliation agreements mostly expire through December 2027, when renewal may raise payments. The forces matter mostly through distribution and programming costs: a loss of leverage in either direction would show in the per-subscriber fee base and in fixed programming costs rather than in volume.
### Regulatory, economic and technology factors

Regulation is a primary credit driver here, so it is assessed: the FCC approved the merger on conditions that include divesting six stations within two years if a local ownership waiver is still needed, with no buyer agreed, and the notice on WPIX alleges an unauthorised transfer of control and proposes a forfeiture and a divestiture that the issuer disputes and cannot estimate; a challenge to the repeal of the national cap could bear on the injunction litigation because the merger relied on a waiver. Economic exposure runs through advertising softness and political crowd-out, with tariffs, inflation and high rates named as risks. Technology matters through streaming, which erodes the subscriber base, and through the next-generation broadcast standard, deployed in stations reaching 50% of households, for which no revenue is stated. Of the three, only regulation can force an asset sale, and the amounts are not established.
### Opportunities and threats

The strengths and weaknesses are set out above. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are a narrowed or lifted injunction that lets cost savings begin, a second year of repayment at the 2026 pace, the renewal of TV Food Network on current terms, and affiliation and retransmission renewals that keep rates ahead of subscriber losses. Threats that could weaken it are an adverse trial outcome that forces a divestiture or continued separation, a forfeiture and divestiture order on WPIX, a rise in MVPD attrition, higher network affiliation fees at the renewals through December 2027, refinancing of the 2027 notes of USD 440 million at higher cost, and the reversion of the covenant limit to 4.25x.
### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and market position are strong: the largest station group by the issuer's description, reaching about 80% of households. Competitive advantage is average, resting on network affiliations and retransmission leverage that depend on renewals through December 2027. Business diversification is average: local advertising is spread over tens of thousands of advertisers and no market exceeds 3% of revenue, but two customers account for 25% of revenue and the business is one industry. Cost and capex flexibility is average, because capital expenditure is low yet operating costs are mostly fixed. Margin stability is weak, given the 94.32% decremental flow-through. Free cash flow stability is average, strong in an election year and unproven in an odd year on the new structure. The ability to refinance is average: markets were open for USD 5,115 million of notes in 2026, but at higher coupons and with 2027 maturities still to address. Liquidity is average, with USD 887 million available and no slack under a zero-cash-flow stress. Financial policy and governance are average, with repayment ahead of buybacks but an unchanged dividend and a board whose composition cannot be tested without the proxy statement. The trend is improving in cash terms and uncertain in earnings quality; the main missing datapoints are the covenant definitions, a post-acquisition odd-year result and peer comparisons.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

In the next 12 to 24 months the fourth quarter of 2026 should be the strongest of the cycle because political advertising peaks, after which 2027 loses it; the covenant election ends after 2026-12-31, the retransmission extension offered under the FCC condition ends on 2026-11-30, the Belo notes of USD 440 million mature on 2027-06-01 and 2027-09-15, the trial opens on 2027-07-06 and the outside synergies date is 2027-09-19. In three to five years the main items are the 2028 notes of USD 1,000 million and the Mission term loan, the 2030 revolver and Term Loan A, the effect of MVPD attrition against streaming growth, and whether deregulation allows further consolidation. Tailwinds are rate escalators, streaming subscriber growth, the completed CBS, FOX, ABC and CW affiliation renewals and any narrowing of the injunction; headwinds are the injunction, the odd-year drop, attrition and rising programming costs. Each supports or pressures cash-flow visibility and refinancing confidence rather than the near-term ability to pay.
### Downside scenario

The scenario starts in a non-election year with the injunction still in force at trial. First, political advertising falls from USD 511 million in the first nine months of 2026 to a residual, and at the FY2025 flow-through the combined business loses USD 423.39 million to USD 458.41 million of Adjusted EBITDA on a nine-month basis, leaving USD 1,401.59 million to USD 1,436.61 million. Second, interest does not fall: the 2026 structure carries about USD 558 million of net interest over nine months at the Q3 pace, so nine-month cover falls to 2.51x to 2.57x from 3.33x at the same interest pace. Third, free cash flow falls by the lost earnings less the tax saved while cash interest rises toward the run-rate of USD 706.83 million to USD 755.95 million a year, and the dividend of about USD 229.29 million a year continues unless cut. Fourth, liquidity of USD 887 million still covers the USD 579 million of principal due by the end of 2027, but not that plus the dividend and the minority put on The CW if free cash flow were zero, so the issuer would need free cash flow, a refinancing of the Belo notes, a dividend cut or the revolver. Fifth, the covenant limit reverts to 4.25x against 3.03x reported, which leaves 1.22x of headroom on the issuer's basis, so on the issuer's ratio a covenant breach is not the first break; the first breaks are interest cover and refinancing cost. Management levers are the dividend, the paused repurchases, capital expenditure, voluntary prepayments and station sales. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027 on positive free cash flow, with limited margin if the court outcome and the odd-year drop coincide. Observable triggers are the ruling after the 2026-11-17 argument, the first two quarters of 2027, any second covenant election and the pricing of the 2027 notes. Primary downside path: a non-election year with the injunction unresolved removes political earnings from a capital structure sized in an election year, so interest cover and refinancing of the 2027 and 2028 maturities become the first constraints.

### Claims outside the debt figure

The debt figure of USD 11,409 million excludes operating lease liabilities of USD 336 million, assumed programming commitments of USD 1,420 million that are not recorded as liabilities, the minority put on The CW with an estimated redemption value of USD 110 million against USD 28 million carried, and standby letters of credit of USD 30 million that reduce revolver availability. Pension and retiree funding is outside it too: Nexstar's own plans were underfunded by USD 154 million at 2025-12-31, the plan assumed from TEGNA carried a net liability of USD 19 million at closing and retiree plan funding obligations were USD 16 million at 2025-12-31. Before the acquisition, at 2025-12-31, Nexstar also had unrecorded commitments of USD 806 million under network affiliation agreements, USD 662 million falling due in 2026 and USD 144 million in 2027 to 2028, and USD 1,008 million of future broadcast rights commitments; these legacy figures sit beside the assumed commitments above and show that affiliation contracts largely run out by 2028, so renewal fees are not yet in them. The debt figure includes Mission's facility of USD 347 million, which Nexstar guarantees. Accrued network affiliation fees of USD 283 million and deferred revenue of USD 123 million are non-debt funding that grew with the acquisition. Litigation and tax items are unquantified: the Chicago Cubs tax matter on which the IRS proposed USD 182 million of tax and a USD 73 million penalty before a Tax Court decision for the company, the 2014 to 2015 audit adjustments, and the class action for money damages. The consent decrees carry no financial penalties. Searches of the filings found no factoring, supply-chain finance or finance lease disclosure.
### Overall credit view

Overall, Nexstar presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, a contractual per-subscriber fee base and low capital intensity, but credit quality is constrained by leverage taken on to buy TEGNA, by earnings that swing with the political cycle and by an integration that a court has blocked. Cash-flow durability appears adequate in election years and not yet established in odd years, because FY2025 showed a near-full flow-through of lost political revenue and the combined company has no odd-year record. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the pace of repayment through the first half of 2027, the outcome of the injunction litigation and the cost at which the 2027 notes and 2028 notes can be refinanced. The primary downside path is a non-election year with the injunction unresolved. No peer set was supplied, so the comparison with typical leveraged issuers in television broadcasting is a judgement: scale and the per-subscriber fee base are the differentiators and leverage at the election-year peak is the offset. Further analysis would require the covenant definitions, any court ruling after 2026-11-17, a post-acquisition odd-year result and peer comparisons. Fundamental credit assessment complete. Top risk: leverage that depends on election-year cash flow.

## Gaps

- High: The credit agreement definitions and compliance certificates are not supplied, so the earnings cushion before the first-lien test would breach is not calculable and the headroom is stated in turns only; the executed documents would close this.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_nxst-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; Source readiness (CP-0)

- High: No post-acquisition odd-year result and no TEGNA odd-year earnings are supplied, so the odd-year cover and the free cash flow in 2027 are sensitivities, not estimates; the fourth-quarter 2026 and first-half 2027 results would close this.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C07
- Medium: Any court ruling after the 2026-11-17 argument is not in the documents, so whether the injunction was narrowed is not established; the downside takes it as continuing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nxst-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33
